title: Context Management
summary: Keeps long agent sessions on track with a running notes file, checkpoints and tightly scoped reads, so quality does not fade as the context fills.
description: Long sessions fail quietly. The agent forgets a decision from two hours ago, rereads the same large files, or repeats an approach that already failed. This skill gives it a small set of habits that keep the important facts outside the context window and the context itself lean.
You end up with a notes file that any fresh session can pick up, so stopping and restarting costs minutes instead of an hour of re-explaining.
useWhen: A task will take more than an hour or touch many files
The agent starts contradicting earlier decisions
You need to hand a half-finished task to a new session
Responses slow down because huge files keep being read in full
body:
# Context management

Put facts on disk, read narrowly, and checkpoint often.

## Steps

1. At the start, create `.agent/notes.md` (add it to `.git/info/exclude` so it is not committed). Write four headings: Goal, Decisions, Done, Next. Fill Goal in the user's words plus the done check.
2. Read narrowly. Search for the symbol or string first, then read only that function or the lines around it. Open a whole file only when you are about to edit most of it. Use `wc -l` before opening anything unfamiliar.
3. Summarize large outputs. For test runs, build logs and diffs, keep the failing lines and counts, not the whole text. Redirect long output to a file and grep it.
4. Record decisions the moment they are made, with the reason: "use the existing retry helper in src/net.ts, because it handles 429". Record failed approaches with the cause, so they are not tried again.
5. Checkpoint after each completed step: update Done and Next, run the relevant tests, and commit when the user wants commits. A checkpoint is safe to resume from.
6. Delegate noisy side work, such as scanning many files, to a subagent and take back only its conclusion.
7. Watch for drift: if you are about to repeat a command, reread the notes first. If the same problem fails twice, stop, write what you know, and propose a different approach.
8. When the session ends or grows heavy, write a handoff block in the notes: current state, exact next command, open questions, and files in flight.

## Rules

- Never paste secrets into the notes.
- Keep the notes under 80 lines. Prune what is no longer true.
- The notes file records facts, not plans you have not decided on.

## Report

At each checkpoint, one line on what is done and what is next.

example.prompt: We are migrating 40 endpoints to the new auth middleware. This will take a while, so keep yourself organized.
example.result: Created .agent/notes.md. Goal: all 40 routes use requireAuth(), tests green. Decisions: keep legacy checkSession for /webhooks, which uses signatures. Done: 12 of 40, routes under /users and /teams. Next: /billing, starting with src/routes/billing/invoices.ts. Failed approach: codemod for route files, it broke 5 with custom wrappers, so edits are manual.

faq.question: Is the notes file committed?
faq.answer: No. It is added to the local git exclude list, so it stays on your machine unless you decide to share it.

faq.question: Does this replace a project memory file like CLAUDE.md?
faq.answer: No. A memory file holds lasting project rules. The notes file holds the state of one task and can be deleted when that task is finished.

access: Writes a notes file under .agent and a line in .git/info/exclude
